subject: Make colour transform into movements along branches

messages.author: 09d96c7bbd39063d
messages.subject: Make colour transform into movements along branches
parts:
Dear Members,

I want to colour my tree B like A such that colours transform into one another along the branches for movements on a time-scaled tree, just like A. How can I do this in ggtree?

Thanks!

messages.author: fa1e85b72b50d60b
messages.subject: Re: Make colour transform into movements along branches
parts:
Hi, 
The key is to use color gradients can be continuous variables
BTW: Welcome to talk in the groups, so that other people with the same problem can see the results of our exchange.

Here is an example. The email attachment is tree.mcc.

library(ggtree)
library(treeio)
library(ggplot2)

## import mcc tree
tree <- read.beast("tree.mcc")

## convert the tree to a tbl_tree
tree_data <- as_tibble(tree)

## have a look at location, they are discrete 
## variables. We need to first replace these discrete 
## variables with continuous variables.
head(tree_data$location,6)

## save oringinal discrete variables
location_s <- tree_data$location

## discrete var can be converted to numerical value by as.factor and as.numetic
## as.factor(location_s)
## > Levels: Fujian Guangdong Guangxi Hebei Henan HongKong Hunan

## to the numerical value
## The locations shown by the numbers here is consistent with the order of levels above
## Hong Kong is the 6th in levels. 6 is HongKong
location_c <- as.numeric(as.factor(location_s))

## Return numeric location to tree
tree_data$location <- location_c

## convert tbl_tree to treedata object
tree_c <- as.treedata(tree_data)

## There are 7 locations, we prepare 7 color
colors <- rainbow(7)
## name color with continue name
names(colors) <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7")

## set continuous = TRUE and use a continue color scale 
## and meaningless continuous legend is removed
tree_plot <- ggtree(tree_c, aes(color=location), size=1.5, continuous = TRUE) + 
  scale_color_gradientn(colours=colors) +
  theme(legend.position="none")
  
## bar plot data
x <- as.data.frame(table(location_s))
x$prop <- prop.table(x$Freq)

# rename colors with discrete name
names(colors) <- levels(as.factor(location_s))

## bar plot
bar_plot <- ggplot(data = x, aes(x = location_s, y = prop, color=NULL, fill = location_s)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  theme(
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = NA), 
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.1), 
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "gray85", size = 0.05, linetype = "dotted"), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA), 
    axis.text = element_text( colour = "black"), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black", angle = 45), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"), 
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA), 
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA)) +
    labs(x = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL)

## create a grid plot
library(grid)

# Extract the legend
legend <- cowplot::get_legend(bar_plot)

## save to pdf
pdf("plot.pdf", paper = "a4r")
print(tree_plot)
vp <- viewport(width = 0.58, height = 0.8, x=.29, y=0.59)
pushViewport(vp)
# legend should not show in this way
print(bar_plot + theme(legend.position = "none"),vp=vp)
vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.58, height = 0.7, x=1.5, y=0)
pushViewport(vp2)
print(grid.draw(legend),vp=vp2)
dev.off()

By the way, the above conversion of tree data is just to help you understand the process. In fact, the code can be written very simply.

library(ggtree)
library(treeio)
library(ggplot2)
tree <- read.beast("tree.mcc")
colors <- rainbow(7)
names(colors) <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7")
ggtree(tree, aes(color=as.numeric(as.factor(location))), size=1.5, continuous = TRUE) +

scale_color_gradientn(colours=colors) +
  theme(legend.position="none")

[1] "#FF0000" "#FFDB00" "#49FF00" "#00FF92" "#0092FF" "#4900FF" "#FF00DB"

You will know that
In fact, rainbow(n) produces a list of colors of hex codes. 
You can specific by c()
such as
colors <- c("#FF0000", "#FFDB00", "#49FF00", "#00FF92", "#0092FF", "#4900FF", "#FF00DB")

## There are 7 locations, we prepare 7 color
colors <- rainbow(7)
## name color with continue name
names(colors) <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7")

## set continuous = TRUE and use a continue color scale 
## and meaningless continuous legend is removed
tree_plot <- ggtree(tree_c, aes(color=location), size=1.5, continuous = TRUE) + 
  scale_color_gradientn(colours=colors) +
  theme(legend.position="none")
  
## bar plot data
x <- as.data.frame(table(location_s))
x$prop <- prop.table(x$Freq)

# rename colors with discrete name
names(colors) <- levels(as.factor(location_s))

## bar plot
bar_plot <- ggplot(data = x, aes(x = location_s, y = prop, color=NULL, fill = location_s)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  theme(
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = NA), 
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.1), 
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "gray85", size = 0.05, linetype = "dotted"), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA), 
    axis.text = element_text( colour = "black"), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black", angle = 45), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"), 
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA), 
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA)) +
    labs(x = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL)

## create a grid plot
library(grid)

# Extract the legend
legend <- cowplot::get_legend(bar_plot)

## save to pdf
pdf("plot.pdf", paper = "a4r")
print(tree_plot)
vp <- viewport(width = 0.58, height = 0.8, x=.29, y=0.59)
pushViewport(vp)
# legend should not show in this way
print(bar_plot + theme(legend.position = "none"),vp=vp)
vp2 <- viewport(width = 0.58, height = 0.7, x=1.5, y=0)
pushViewport(vp2)
print(grid.draw(legend),vp=vp2)
dev.off()

You can specific by c()

Hi, 
The key is to use color gradients can be continuous variables
BTW: Welcome to talk in the groups, so that other people with the same problem can see the results of our exchange.

Here is an example. The email attachment is tree.mcc.

library(ggtree)
library(treeio)
library(ggplot2)

## import mcc tree
tree <- read.beast("tree.mcc")

## convert the tree to a tbl_tree
tree_data <- as_tibble(tree)

## have a look at location, they are discrete 
## variables. We need to first replace these discrete 
## variables with continuous variables.
head(tree_data$location,6)

## save oringinal discrete variables
location_s <- tree_data$location

## discrete var can be converted to numerical value by as.factor and as.numetic
## as.factor(location_s)
## > Levels: Fujian Guangdong Guangxi Hebei Henan HongKong Hunan

## to the numerical value
## The locations shown by the numbers here is consistent with the order of levels above
## Hong Kong is the 6th in levels. 6 is HongKong
location_c <- as.numeric(as.factor(location_s))

## Return numeric location to tree
tree_data$location <- location_c

## convert tbl_tree to treedata object
tree_c <- as.treedata(tree_data)

## There are 7 locations, we prepare 7 color
colors <- rainbow(7)
## name color with continue name
names(colors) <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7")

## set continuous = TRUE and use a continue color scale 
## and meaningless continuous legend is removed
tree_plot <- ggtree(tree_c, aes(color=location), size=1.5, continuous = TRUE) + 
  scale_color_gradientn(colours=colors) +
  theme(legend.position="none")
  
## bar plot data
x <- as.data.frame(table(location_s))
x$prop <- prop.table(x$Freq)

# rename colors with discrete name
names(colors) <- levels(as.factor(location_s))

## bar plot
bar_plot <- ggplot(data = x, aes(x = location_s, y = prop, color=NULL, fill = location_s)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
  theme(
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = NA), 
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.1), 
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "gray85", size = 0.05, linetype = "dotted"), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = NA), 
    axis.text = element_text( colour = "black"), 
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, colour = "black", angle = 45), 
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "black"), 
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA), 
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA)) +
    labs(x = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL)

## create a grid plot

# Extract the legend

## save to pdf
pdf("plot.pdf", paper = "a4r")
